angles: Sim Studio (now rebranded to 'Sim') has evolved from a simple workflow GUI into a full AI workspace with Mothership natural-language control plane
Unlike n8n's fair-code license, Sim is fully Apache-2.0 licensed — a key differentiator for open-source purists
Sim's Mothership feature lets users describe systems in natural language and auto-generates workflows, tables, and knowledge bases
The visual workflow builder is not just for prototyping — it's the actual execution engine with simulation, observability, and deployment capabilities
Sim's rapid release cadence (near-daily releases) shows aggressive development pace compared to competitors
Self-hosting is free with no execution limits — a major selling point over n8n's paid tiers
Sim positions itself as an 'AI workspace' rather than just a workflow tool, combining agents, knowledge bases, tables, and files in one environment
The project went from zero to 29K stars in 18 months — one of the fastest-growing open-source AI tools
